tiers.label: Basic laptop, 8 GB memory
tiers.hint: Small models only. Fine for short questions, summaries and translating; slow on long texts.

tiers.label: 16 GB memory or 16 GB Mac
tiers.hint: The sweet spot for most people: good everyday answers at a comfortable speed. The 8 GB picks run here too, faster.

tiers.label: 32 GB or 12-16 GB graphics card
tiers.hint: Room for the strongest models that still fit one normal computer. Everything from the smaller sizes also runs.

tiers.label: 24 GB graphics card or 48-64 GB Mac
tiers.hint: Gaming-class graphics card (RTX 3090, 4090, 5090) or a high-memory Mac. Fast replies from the 32 GB picks, plus these larger ones.

tiers.label: Workstation, 96 GB or more
tiers.hint: The biggest open models. Closest to the paid chatbots, but they need serious hardware.

models.name: Qwen 3.5 4B
models.plain: The best all-rounder that fits a small laptop. Answers questions, summarizes, and can look at pictures.

models.name: Gemma 4 E2B
models.plain: Google's smallest Gemma, built for laptops and phones. Friendly writing style, reads images.

models.name: Ministral 3 3B
models.plain: A small European model that is good with many languages and quick on modest hardware.

models.name: Granite 4.2 3B
models.plain: The lightest pick here. Quick summaries and answers about documents, text only.

models.name: Gemma 4 12B
models.plain: The most capable everyday model for a 16 GB computer: writing, questions, and understanding images.

models.name: Qwen 3.5 9B
models.plain: A strong general model that leaves memory free for other apps. Good with code and many languages.

models.name: Ministral 3 14B
models.plain: The largest Ministral. Handles long documents and European languages well.

models.name: LFM2.5 8B
models.plain: Built for speed on ordinary hardware and for assistants that use tools. Text only.

models.name: Qwen 3.8 27B
models.plain: The strongest open model that still fits one good computer. Code, research and long tasks.

models.name: Gemma 4 26B
models.plain: Polished writing and image understanding, with long documents in one go.

models.name: gpt-oss 20B
models.plain: OpenAI's free model that thinks step by step before answering. Text only.

models.name: Devstral Small 2
models.plain: Made for programming: reads a whole project, edits several files, works with coding tools.

models.name: Muse Glimmer 30B
models.plain: Meta's model for assistants that run all day and use tools on your behalf.

models.name: Gemma 4 31B
models.plain: The largest Gemma. Best writing quality you can fit on a single graphics card.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 35B
models.plain: Tuned for coding agents: works through a whole repository and keeps its reasoning between steps.

models.name: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
models.plain: Very fast for its size and reads huge amounts of text at once. Needs a 48 GB Mac or two cards.

models.name: gpt-oss 120B
models.plain: OpenAI's large free model. Careful step-by-step reasoning, text only.

models.name: Qwen 3.5 122B
models.plain: A big general model that also reads images. Strong across languages.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.5
models.license: Modified MIT (limits for very large companies)
models.plain: Mistral's flagship: instructions, reasoning and code in one model, with image input.
